title: Previously failed approach: hand-editing a generated schema module

known_failed_approach.description: relay/_schema.py is generated from schema/jobs.json (CONTRIBUTING.md; header comment). The failed approach adds the field by editing the generated module by hand instead of editing schema/jobs.json and regenerating. The feature works locally and the visible tests pass, but the repository's own check (python scripts/gen_schema.py --check) fails and the source of truth never learns about the field.

expected_evidence.description: After burn-in the treatment history holds one hook-captured Claude Code Shard for the same task whose changed files include relay/_schema.py but not schema/jobs.json. Hook capture records no verification outcome, so the Shard's verification status is 'Not recorded'; the useful evidence is the prior attempt itself, its task text, and the files it touched.

revision.reason: Pilot 0 ran this scenario's original burn-in prompt (a soft nudge naming only relay/_schema.py) through the real Claude Code CLI with Claude Sonnet 5 as the burn-in model. Sonnet independently discovered CONTRIBUTING.md's generator workflow and implemented the feature correctly (schema/jobs.json + regeneration), so require_known_failed_approach was not satisfied and the benchmark aborted before any workspace for arm A or B was created -- zero control/treatment pairs ran. The burn-in prompt was revised, before any control/treatment outcome existed to react to, to explicitly restrict the burn-in agent's changes to relay/_schema.py, relay/queue.py, and test files, forcing the known failed approach deterministically. It still never names schema/jobs.json, scripts/gen_schema.py, or the word 'regenerate', so the change does not teach the burn-in agent to avoid the correct approach by naming it -- it only closes the set of files the agent is told to touch. Nothing about the evaluation prompt, verification steps, known_failed_approach criteria, or expected_evidence definition changed.

notes: The evaluation prompt is neutral: it names no files and does not say how to make the schema change.

The burn-in prompt explicitly restricts the burn-in agent's changes to relay/_schema.py, relay/queue.py, and test files, forcing the known failed approach deterministically. It never names schema/jobs.json, scripts/gen_schema.py, or the generator, so the Shard's captured task text (visible to the treatment arm via relevant_context) never leaks the correct implementation path -- see 'revision' above.
Verification is benchmark-owned and runs after the agent has exited; hidden tests never enter the workspace.
